messages:
support-alex: FYI customers on hosted are seeing intermittent 504s and long tail latencies for several tenants (Foodly + 2 others). Started ~09:40 UTC, repeatable spike when concurrency > ~80. Raised ticket #INC-9842 :rotating_light:

support-jordan: Can you paste an example request id or trace_id? Need to attach to the ticket and notify SEs.

support-alex: trace_id=trc-0b7d3f5a, sample logs below:
```
[2026-03-17T09:41:02Z] INFO incoming_request id=trc-0b7d3f5a customer=foodly path=/v1/generate model=redwood-13b seq_len=512
[2026-03-17T09:41:02Z] WARN enqueue request_queue_len=2048 request_queue_limit=2048 route=hosted-ingress
[2026-03-17T09:41:02Z] ERROR dequeue_timeout id=trc-0b7d3f5a wait_ms=120000 batcher_id=batcher-7 reason=continuous-batcher-backlog
[2026-03-17T09:41:02Z] ERROR gateway_504 id=trc-0b7d3f5a status=504
```

sam-eng: Looks like request_queue_len is pegged at the configured limit (2048). Dequeue rate drops when continuous-batcher backlog grows because of lots of long seq_len requests. That explains tail timeouts.

maria-sre: Are these tenants using the same model variant and no per-tenant throttles? Also check if prefix caching is cold which increases decode time per request.

liz-ops: I pulled metrics from the last 30m: host-group us-west-2a avg_dequeue_rate=18r/s but incoming_rate=95r/s during spike; batcher-latency p95 jumped from 120ms -> 2.1s. KVcache-miss rate increased ~30%.

support-jordan: Customer reports they sent a burst of high-concurrency load from a marketing campaign, concurrency ~150 sustained for ~3m. They were not aware of rate limits.

sam-eng: Repro steps we used in staging: run k6 with 120 concurrent users, payloads with seq_len=1024, model=redwood-13b, connections=200. Reproduces request_queue hitting limit and 504s in ~90s. Command snippet:
```
k6 run --vus 120 --duration 3m script.js --env MODEL=redwood-13b
```

maria-sre: Immediate mitigations: 1) temporarily increase request_queue_limit to 4096 on affected host-group, 2) enable early_reject for requests older than 10s, 3) spin up 2 extra batcher pods (scale batcher deployment +20%).

liz-ops: On it — will push queue_limit bump and scale batchers. Pushing now, ETA ~2m.

deploy-bot: build/ops deploy started by liz-ops for config/hosted/queue_limit -> 4096 (deploy-id: dpl-773b)

liz-ops: Done. queue_limit=4096 applied, batcher replicas +2. Watching metrics.

support-alex: Customer reporting improvement, 504s dropped from ~12/min -> ~1/min after the change. They still see a few slow tails.

sam-eng: Next actions: 1) add per-tenant soft throttles for sudden bursts (rate-limit tokens), 2) implement smarter eviction (drop_oldest for low-priority tenants), 3) add autoscale trigger on backlog_ratio > 0.6 for continuous-batcher. Filed follow-up engineering ticket ENG-1987.

maria-sre: Also recommend we add a short-term alert: request_queue_len / request_queue_limit > 0.8 sustained for 30s -> P1 page.

support-jordan: I'll update ticket INC-9842 with timeline, mitigation steps, and customer note.

support-alex: Customer says they can throttle. We'll coordinate to apply client-side backoff + reattempt strategy.

sam-eng: For the record, root cause = request queue saturation caused by an unexpected burst of long-sequence requests causing continuous-batcher backlog and KV cache churn, causing dequeue to stall and some requests to exceed dequeue timeout -> 504.

liz-ops: Closing immediate incident. Keeping ENG and SRE follow-ups open.

support-jordan: Thanks team, adding postmortem notes and customer follow-up plan. :thumbsup:
